title: dragon nest
text: It truly breaks my heart giving this game a negative review. This game used to be my most favorite MMORPG, simply from its action-oriented and non-targetting combat style, w/ its good community (from what I saw). Don't be misjudged by my hours of playtime, I had to run it on Nexon as for some reason the steam version never worked for me. So, what's so bad about it now? For starters, the playerbase is basically dead. I predict a few more months or maybe some years, and the game will be completely dried out of players. If you're new, wanting to play, you most likely won't come across anyone who will play w/ you as most are just lvl 90+, and have no interest in doing such little tasks for a person who will inevitably get bored and leave. That brings me to my next point: The level cap. Before, the level cap was 60-70, a good level cap for this game in my opinion. However, apparently from the time I was on hiatus until recently, they've changed the cap to 93 (I think) So, instead of fun dungeon-crawling with random people or guild-mates, you're stuck basically grinding alone in a dead server to reach 93 and get some actual good stuff. 3-4 years ago, this game WAS MY LIFE. I would NOT stop gawking about it to friends, trying to get them to play, then them join and have a blast w/ me. Now? Now it's a dead place with hardly any chat in global andno one to dungeon crawl with (which, people to hang out with was one of the best parts, and grinding to such a level on your own would eventually wear you out). Just that, is enough to pull me away from this. Now something for all those verteran players like me, that kinda set us off. Apparently, around september 2016 and before, you could switch your account to EYEDenity (Nexon had control over DN first, then it was switched to Eyedenity). HOWEVER, if you didn't transfer it between that deadline, all your content was erased. Yep. MEANING, If you have a lvl 70 character, with some REALLY good gear, and you payed REAL LIFE Money on the game, that was all for nothing, as it was erased on the transfer. Granted, I never spent a dime on it, but it aggitated me, trying to use my Nexon account, finding out it wont work, and having that ONE Character I spent hours upon hours to get to lvl 50 with a single friend, which the file had a lot of memories for me. It's a sad tale, a wonderful game turned into.... this. Sorry to say, but I can't recommend it :(.

text: This game is like League of Legends but with dragons instead of various humanoids and monsters. Shortly after the tutorial it will pitch a Titan Pass to you. The difference between winning and loosing in PVP depends upon your tactics as well as the tactics of your teammates. But if PVP isnt your style then you can join with others to battle some BOTS in a much more lenient, comfortable setting. There are other game modes also, so the game stays interesting. All in all im giving this game 9.5/10. Very well made and original. The selection of dragons alone is impressive and this game has more to offer than just that.

title: duke nukem forever
text: To me this game doesn't try to be anything but a good time and to me it delivered.  There’s no epic story, no customization, no ability points, just mindless abiet linear guided A+ FUN!  The game’s combat and strategy/tactics weren’t very rich yet the linear journey from beginning stage to end stage contained all sorts of flair and one liners that gave me enjoyment. I liked killing aliens and hearing Duke say "my balls, your face" or "When you get into hell tell them Duke sent you" etc... I thought being shrunk at Duke's burger and navigating the kitchen reading food labels was a blast.  Shrinking aliens and stomping them also fuN! I enjoyed the first hour where the setting shows Duke as a revered hero from 12 years ago living in a penthouse suite with babes.  I thought the various interaction in the environment were neat and interesting.  There's also a stage when you’re in a helicopter shooting aliens and a metal cover of "rise of the Valkyries by Wagner” is played.  It was just TOO COOL for ME! To me it was a polished experience.  Lots of small details to notice that brought joy. I think I understand the mixed reviews.  I did get a sense that this could have been a REALLY AWESOME game but instead it’s just good and maybe a bit niche with the macho-ism.  It seems like it was marketed as an A+ block buster and yeah if I had to pay $60 for it I wouldn’t recommend it. I got it cheap and don’t regret that!

title: duke nukem forever
text: It's normal to have high expectations on a game that's been in development for more than 10 years, but to judge it it's important to know a little of its development history to understand why they took so long to finish it. It was remade from scratch many times because of the engine or graphics being outdated, they wanted it to be perfect, or at least as groundbreaking as the original Duke Nukem 3D was at its time. Due to this fact, many of the original ideas planned for the game didn't make it to the final product as can be seen in its many trailers. But then, when all hope was lost (with 3D Realms closing) Gearbox appeared and saved the day buying the Duke Nukem license. And then the game was released. Was it groundbreaking? No. Was it awesome? I wish... Was it bad? No, and that's what it's important. If you don't know the history of its development, the final product (at least the bulk of it, not counting the makeup and multiplayer Gearbox added later) was finished by 2009, and due to budget and legal problems, the game felt a little old even for that time. So probably most of its ideas were nice and new for 2005 maybe, its not bad! But not as impactating as they wish they were (if they decided to change it, it probably would have never been released). Plot wise, it isn't something jaw dropping, it is something you would expect from a Duke Nukem game: Duke is loved and desired by the women, men admire him, and kids want to be like him, it's all going well until an alien mothership comes to Earth. The problem is, they're not being hostile... yet. As the story unfolds (doesn't take too long actually) everybody finds out that the aliens plan on abducting the women, and kill everyone else, ESPECIALLY Duke Nukem, so it's up to the King to go rescue the babes and save the world once again. Graphically, it isn't outstanding by any means, but Gearbox did a really good job poilishing it, the blur and depth of filed effects are really well implemented. You can notice a few low res texture here and there (most noticeable on the console versions) but it shines at times like in the Cycloid Emperor fight at the start of the game or in the Mothership battle a bit alter on. What really is kinda of ugly, it's the animations, the characters move unnaturally and don't have many facial expressions, reminded of Quake 4 NPCs. On the other hand, the enemies are very detailed and in general really well done. In the Sound department, it lacks a more compelling soundtrack, but the voice acting is really well done, Jon St. John returns as Duke doing a really great job. The other NPCs sound a little ridiculous sometimes, but that's intended. The one-liners return and (fortunately for me and unfortunately for others) the old ones come back too. There aren't many good ones within the introduced in this game, but some really have the spirit of the franchise. Gameplay was one of the most controversial things about this game, I thought it was too linear run and gun with regenerative health (ego) as most FPS games are nowadays, and that's what disappointed me. Don't get me wrong, it's fun to play, but I expected it to be more open ended like Duke 3D. I was hoping for something that would really differ (in a good way) from all the games we have today. There are puzzles here and there and I enjoyed them, to reduce the pace a little to not get too repetitive. The other games references were funny and not offensive like most people think they were, Duke Nukem 3D featured a "dead space marine.." (Duke's voice) and played just like it, guys at Id found it hilarious and not offensive, it's more of a homage than an offense. The guns for the most part don't feel very powerful (with the exception of the shotgun), and the classic funny ones can't be used as they were in Duke 3D because of the 2 weapon limit (4 as an option with a later released patch), the Shrink Ray is overpowered, since it's almost One Shot One Kill, but the Freeze-Ray is underpowered because it takes a lot of time to actually freeze the enemy and puts you in harm's way since it only works in close range. The loading times aren't as huge on the PC as they are on the console versions, but it is still a little big when you are dying constantly in a specific part of the game. You can't save whenever you want, instead the game uses checkpoints, which actually makes the game more challenging (too much at times but oh well). Multiplayer is old school. Features deathmatch, team deathmatch, CTF (CT Babe in this case), and King of The Hill. All old school fast paced, not many people play it, but its fun for a while. Weird that when any player dies, they blow up instead of having ragdolls, probably because the guys at Gearbox didn't have time to implement it. As a game released these days, I'll give it a 6, which is fair, it shares a lot of similarities to other popular FPS games these days (including the complaints). But knowing that it was supposed to be released a long time ago (talking of the actual build, not the old ones), when the ideas were actually "new" for the time, I would give it a 7.8. I think that after all that the developers been through, they deserve a little understanding.

title: dungeon defenders
text: I haven't played this game in a while but it is my highest played game in my library, so I felt it deserved a review. This is definitely a game that is best played with friends but even solo it is still a very fun game. It is a perfect mix of tower defense and monster slaying combined for a great expereince. There are tons of maps you can play, even in the base game without DLC, and each map has different levels for the different diffuculties, up to a nightmare mode (which I've never been able to beat but on the easiest map). There is a strategic mix of weapons and armor combinations, or you could just slap some together and make it work, it allows for either option, of course more benefits come from working with the armor and building a set that matches your play style. There are also lots of heroes you can play and they all offer a variety of skills and towers you can build for defense. When you really get into it you can have a character of each type and level them all, and use their skills together so even if you are playing solo you aren't missing out on the great abilities of characters.

Every other class can not solo end game well enough without the best of the best gear, and even then, it's probably impossible. So, broken classes (Squire is better than everything by far) + a broken business model (charging people for the game for over a year and then suddenly making it free to play, prioritizing skins and selling in-game currency over actually progressing the game to a conclusion and taking it out of Early Access) + broken servers (lagging in my private tavern, connecting to the public tavern happens once in a while) = not recommended.
